calas:Ayazma.name: Ayazma
calas:Ayazma.hook: The island's busiest beach — fine golden sand and turquoise water, loungers and a row of fish-and-meze restaurants for a sunset beer.
calas:Ayazma.text: The island's busiest beach — fine golden sand and turquoise water, loungers and a row of fish-and-meze restaurants for a sunset beer. Named for the 1734 Aya Paraskevi monastery and its holy spring behind it ( ayazma = Greek hagiasma , holy water), which opens once a year on 26 July for the saint's-day pilgrimage. Best on a north (poyraz) wind; arrive before 10am in July–August or there is no sand left. Free + paid loungers, south coast · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Habbele (Poyraz Limanı).name: Habbele (Poyraz Limanı)
calas:Habbele (Poyraz Limanı).hook: The closest swimmable cove to town and the family pick — a bowl-shaped bay so calm even a poyraz can't roughen it, the warmest, shallowest water on the island.
calas:Habbele (Poyraz Limanı).text: The closest swimmable cove to town and the family pick — a bowl-shaped bay so calm even a poyraz can't roughen it, the warmest, shallowest water on the island. Golden sand with a paid lounger section at one end and a free pitch-your-own stretch at the other. Watch for sea urchins on the bottom — wear water shoes. Free + paid, closest to town · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Sulubahçe.name: Sulubahçe
calas:Sulubahçe.hook: Ayazma's quiet neighbour: the same crystal water and good sand, but no loungers and no café, so it keeps its natural character — and its campers.
calas:Sulubahçe.text: Ayazma's quiet neighbour: the same crystal water and good sand, but no loungers and no café, so it keeps its natural character — and its campers. Rocky shelves at the eastern end draw snorkellers. Like Ayazma it wants a north wind and is exposed when the lodos turns. No facilities, bring everything · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Akvaryum (Aquarium Cove).name: Akvaryum (Aquarium Cove)
calas:Akvaryum (Aquarium Cove).hook: An east-coast cove named for water so clear you can count the fish — the island's snorkelling spot, and the one that comes into its own on a south (lodos) wind.
calas:Akvaryum (Aquarium Cove).text: An east-coast cove named for water so clear you can count the fish — the island's snorkelling spot, and the one that comes into its own on a south (lodos) wind. No sunbeds, showers or changing rooms; the access track is rough, so park at the roadside and walk the last fifteen minutes (or take the summer shuttle). Snorkelling, no facilities · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Çayır.name: Çayır
calas:Çayır.hook: The windy beach, deliberately — a flat, exposed north-side point that catches the full poyraz, which makes it the island's windsurf and kitesurf centre rather than a place to swim calm.
calas:Çayır.text: The windy beach, deliberately — a flat, exposed north-side point that catches the full poyraz, which makes it the island's windsurf and kitesurf centre rather than a place to swim calm. It hosted the European Kitesurf Championship in 2015 and has a kite school on site; the swimmers go elsewhere, the boards come here. Windsurf / kite, not calm swimming · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Tuzburnu.name: Tuzburnu
calas:Tuzburnu.hook: A remote rocky cove at the western tip below the lighthouse and windmills, reachable only by car with no facilities at all.
calas:Tuzburnu.text: A remote rocky cove at the western tip below the lighthouse and windmills, reachable only by car with no facilities at all. The water is clear but colder than the south-coast sand; the draw is rocky swimming and a noted sunset rather than comfort. Remote, rocky, a sunset cove · Open in Google Maps →

walks:Göztepe — the panorama.name: Göztepe — the panorama
walks:Göztepe — the panorama.hook: The island's highest point at 192 m, on foot only — about half an hour gently up from the centre.
walks:Göztepe — the panorama.text: The island's highest point at 192 m, on foot only — about half an hour gently up from the centre. You cannot drive up; the payoff is a genuine 360-degree sweep over vineyards, pine, the windmills and the offshore islets. Go for sunrise or late afternoon, not midday. ~30 min up, on foot only · Open in Google Maps →

walks:The castle ramparts.name: The castle ramparts
walks:The castle ramparts.hook: Walk the walls of the 1455 fortress for the full town-and-harbour view.
walks:The castle ramparts.text: Walk the walls of the 1455 fortress for the full town-and-harbour view. Bailey, citadel and the dry landward moat; floodlit after dark, when the walls and the masts in the harbour light up together. Inside the castle ticket · Open in Google Maps →

walks:The vineyard country.name: The vineyard country
walks:The vineyard country.hook: Vines cover much of the interior — the island's defining inland walk, gentle open country between Göztepe and the south coast.
walks:The vineyard country.text: Vines cover much of the interior — the island's defining inland walk, gentle open country between Göztepe and the south coast. The respected producers are Corvus, Talay, Çamlıbağ (Yunatçılar) and Ataol; several can be tasted in town, but the walk between the rows is the point. Open country; carry water · Open in Google Maps →

walks:Polente at sunset.name: Polente at sunset
walks:Polente at sunset.hook: A real walk — reckon an hour from the centre, past the wind turbines to the bare western cape and the 1861 lighthouse.
walks:Polente at sunset.text: A real walk — reckon an hour from the centre, past the wind turbines to the bare western cape and the 1861 lighthouse. Farther than it looks and with no shade, so carry water; the reward is the island's sunset gathering, the old light against the turbine ridge. ~1 hr each way; no shade · Open in Google Maps →

walks:The Ayazma plane-tree walk.name: The Ayazma plane-tree walk
walks:The Ayazma plane-tree walk.hook: On the wooded south side, a shaded counterpoint to the bare west.
walks:The Ayazma plane-tree walk.text: On the wooded south side, a shaded counterpoint to the bare west. The 1734 chapel sits under eight old plane trees beside a constantly flowing two-spout fountain and its holy spring — cool, green, and quiet outside the 26 July pilgrimage. Shaded; near Ayazma beach · Open in Google Maps →

coffee-gardens:Çınaraltı Café.name: Çınaraltı Café
coffee-gardens:Çınaraltı Café.hook: Trading since 1969 under a giant plane tree — its name means ‘under the plane tree’.
coffee-gardens:Çınaraltı Café.text: Trading since 1969 under a giant plane tree — its name means ‘under the plane tree’. The slow, shaded spot for a Turkish coffee or tea over the harbour, the way the island has taken its coffee for fifty years. A drink and the shade, not a desk. A drink, not a laptop · Open in Google Maps →

coffee-gardens:Coffee Shelter.name: Coffee Shelter
coffee-gardens:Coffee Shelter.hook: For an actual proper coffee — iced americano, espresso, flat white — the island's most consistently rated coffeehouse, on Çınar Çeşme Sokak.
coffee-gardens:Coffee Shelter.text: For an actual proper coffee — iced americano, espresso, flat white — the island's most consistently rated coffeehouse, on Çınar Çeşme Sokak. The third-wave stop when the plane-tree Turkish coffee isn't what you're after; small, central, busy April–October. Specialty coffee; central · Open in Google Maps →

coffee-gardens:Vasil Coffee & Bakery.name: Vasil Coffee & Bakery
coffee-gardens:Vasil Coffee & Bakery.hook: Turkish coffee and Aegean handmade bakes in the old quarter.
coffee-gardens:Vasil Coffee & Bakery.text: Turkish coffee and Aegean handmade bakes in the old quarter. A bakery-and-coffee room in the Rum lanes — pair the coffee with the island's almond and mastic bakes rather than treat it as a workroom. Coffee + island bakes · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Bozcaada Castle (Tenedos Fortres.name: Bozcaada Castle (Tenedos Fortress)
culture:Bozcaada Castle (Tenedos Fortres.hook: The harbour fortress rebuilt for Mehmet II in 1455 over Phoenician, Venetian and Genoese foundations.
culture:Bozcaada Castle (Tenedos Fortres.text: The harbour fortress rebuilt for Mehmet II in 1455 over Phoenician, Venetian and Genoese foundations. A waterside stronghold of bailey, citadel and dry landward moat guarding the strait. Walk the ramparts for the town-and-harbour view; it is floodlit after dark. Earlier works on the site were demolished after the 14th-century War of Chioggia between Venice and Genoa. Modest ticket; the harbour-view walk · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Church of St Mary — Kimisis Theo.name: Church of St Mary — Kimisis Theotokou
culture:Church of St Mary — Kimisis Theo.hook: The island's last working Greek Orthodox church, built 1869 in the Rum quarter.
culture:Church of St Mary — Kimisis Theo.text: The island's last working Greek Orthodox church, built 1869 in the Rum quarter. A three-aisled nave divided by five Corinthian-capitalled columns, under a four-storey bell tower of 1895 visible from almost anywhere in town — the standing heart of a community that has all but gone. Active church; respect services · Open in Google Maps →

culture:The Rum (Greek) Quarter.name: The Rum (Greek) Quarter
culture:The Rum (Greek) Quarter.hook: Narrow lanes and bougainvillea-draped stone houses below the bell tower.
culture:The Rum (Greek) Quarter.text: Narrow lanes and bougainvillea-draped stone houses below the bell tower. The living trace of a Greek community that once numbered close to 2,000 and now counts about twenty, most having left amid 20th-century state pressure. The restored guesthouses, galleries and wine bars cluster here. A walking quarter, not a ticket · Open in Google Maps →

culture:The Stone Windmills (Yel Değirme.name: The Stone Windmills (Yel Değirmenleri)
culture:The Stone Windmills (Yel Değirme.hook: Cylindrical stone windmills on the high ground that once ground the island's wheat.
culture:The Stone Windmills (Yel Değirme.text: Cylindrical stone windmills on the high ground that once ground the island's wheat. Bozcaada had about a dozen; most fell to ruin as mechanical mills took over, and three were rebuilt in 2019 with domed roofs and white sail-frames — a 10–15 minute walk up from town for a view back over castle and harbour. Free; a short uphill walk · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Polente Lighthouse.name: Polente Lighthouse
culture:Polente Lighthouse.hook: A 32-metre lighthouse of 1861 at the western tip, its light reaching beyond 15 nautical miles.
culture:Polente Lighthouse.text: A 32-metre lighthouse of 1861 at the western tip, its light reaching beyond 15 nautical miles. The island's traditional sunset spot, on the bare western cape — the old light set against the ridge of modern wind turbines that now generate the island's power. A real walk or a short drive from the centre. Free; the sunset cape · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Ayazma Monastery & Holy Spring.name: Ayazma Monastery & Holy Spring
culture:Ayazma Monastery & Holy Spring.hook: A modest Greek Orthodox chapel under plane trees beside a twin-spouted holy spring, near Ayazma beach.
culture:Ayazma Monastery & Holy Spring.text: A modest Greek Orthodox chapel under plane trees beside a twin-spouted holy spring, near Ayazma beach. Closed for most of the year, it opens for the 26 July (Aya Paraskevi) pilgrimage — the spring that gives the beach its name. A shaded, cool counterpoint to the bare western cape. Mostly closed; opens 26 July · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Bozcaada Local History Museum.name: Bozcaada Local History Museum
culture:Bozcaada Local History Museum.hook: A private island museum, opened 2005 by the collector Hakan Gürüney.
culture:Bozcaada Local History Museum.text: A private island museum, opened 2005 by the collector Hakan Gürüney. Fossils, archaeological pieces, coins, maps, old island wine bottles and Greek-and-Turkish household goods gathered into a central historic building — an hour out of the wind, and the quickest way to read the island's layers. Modest admission; central · Open in Google Maps →

gastronomy:The wine route.name: The wine route
gastronomy:The wine route.hook: Half the island is under vine, dry-farmed by the same meltem that turns the wind farm — the route is small enough to ride in a day.
gastronomy:The wine route.text: Half the island is under vine, dry-farmed by the same meltem that turns the wind farm — the route is small enough to ride in a day. Four native grakes carry it: white Çavuş and Vasilaki, red Karalahna and Kuntra. The producers to know are Corvus, Talay, Çamlıbağ and Ataol; because the cellar doors, the harbour and the vines sit in one walkable town, the island itself is the route. Cellar doors in town + the vines · Open in Google Maps →

gastronomy:Bağ Bozumu — the harvest fest.name: Bağ Bozumu — the harvest festival
gastronomy:Bağ Bozumu — the harvest fest.hook: The grape-harvest festival, run every first week of September since 1999.
gastronomy:Bağ Bozumu — the harvest fest.text: The grape-harvest festival, run every first week of September since 1999. Growers still bring the picking in by tractor, horse and donkey to the town square for wine competitions, a ‘best Çavuş’ judging and a Miss Grape contest — the one week the island’s defining crop is in your hand, not a bottle. First week of September · Open in Google Maps →

gastronomy:The Wednesday produce market.name: The Wednesday produce market
gastronomy:The Wednesday produce market.hook: A fruit-and-vegetable market for locals, set up every Wednesday — distinct from the year-round tourist stalls.
gastronomy:The Wednesday produce market.text: A fruit-and-vegetable market for locals, set up every Wednesday — distinct from the year-round tourist stalls. The day to buy island tomatoes, fruit and the famous Çavuş grapes at source rather than from the souvenir shelves; bring cash. Wednesdays; bring cash · Open in Google Maps →
